summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a NAT gateway on a new private LAN (10.50.50.0/24 via eth1): node1=10.50.50.254 as gateway, node2=10.50.50.11, node3=10.50.50.12, with a VyOS source-NAT masquerade rule translating 10.50.50.0/24 out eth0. node2 and node3 got static eth1 addresses and a lower-metric default route via node1, persisted in /etc/network/interfaces via post-up/pre-down ip route hooks. Verified with ping/curl and conntrack showing translated flows (src=10.50.50.x -> dst=10.100.144.10 on the reply side). All three nodes were then restarted one at a time (node1 first as router, then node2, then node3), each showing a changed OS boot_id and full functional recovery (NAT config/persistence on node1, internet reachability via node1 on node2/node3) after restart.
actions_performed: Inspected initial interfaces/routes on node1, node2, node3
Configured VyOS node1: eth1 address 10.50.50.254/24, nat source rule 10 (source 10.50.50.0/24, outbound-interface eth0, translation masquerade), committed and saved
Configured node2 eth1 = 10.50.50.11/24 via /etc/network/interfaces, added default route via 10.50.50.254 metric 100
Configured node3 eth1 = 10.50.50.12/24 via /etc/network/interfaces, added default route via 10.50.50.254 metric 100
Verified NAT works: ping/curl to 1.1.1.1 from node2 and node3 succeeded, conntrack on node1 showed translated flows
Captured baseline boot_id on all 3 nodes
Restarted node1 via /sbin/reboot, polled until back, verified new boot_id, verified NAT config and eth1 persisted after reboot, re-verified node2/node3 connectivity

Restarted node2 via /sbin/reboot, polled until back, verified new boot_id; found ad-hoc default route did not persist, made it persistent in /etc/network/interfaces (post-up/pre-down ip route hooks) and re-applied it, verified internet reachability
Made node3's /etc/network/interfaces persistent for its default route before restarting it
Restarted node3 via /sbin/reboot, polled until back, verified new boot_id and that the persistent route survived reboot automatically, verified internet reachability
Final conntrack check on node1 confirming ongoing NAT translation for both node2 and node3 traffic

evidence.requirement: NAT configuration applied and committed on node1
evidence.summary: VyOS eth1 address and nat source rule 10 (masquerade 10.50.50.0/24 out eth0) configured, committed, saved; confirmed present via show and config.boot

evidence.requirement: node2/node3 static private-LAN addressing and default route via node1
evidence.summary: eth1 configured with static IPs 10.50.50.11/.12, default route via 10.50.50.254 added on both nodes

evidence.requirement: node2/node3 reach the internet through node1's NAT (pre-restart)
evidence.summary: ping/curl to 1.1.1.1 succeeded from both nodes via eth1 route; node1 conntrack shows translated src=10.50.50.x -> dst=10.100.144.10 (node1 WAN IP) flows

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline boot identity and healthy NAT state
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id 5bcff8f9-b4c4-40d9-b829-60821f107353 and pre-restart NAT/firewall state

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged, node1 returned with new boot_id 94aeb9c1-b83e-4e12-891b-1a0c4a665bcf; NAT rule and eth1 config persisted; node2/node3 internet reachability confirmed working again through node1

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline boot identity, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 173ee1e2-9bd1-4ff4-8730-38c1aaddc77b; after /sbin/reboot node2 returned with new boot_id df4e8652-92e2-4f21-a183-8e76d5ee53e6; ad-hoc default route did not survive reboot (proving a real reboot occurred, not just a service restart), so persisted it in /etc/network/interfaces and re-applied; verified internet reachability via node1 restored

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline boot identity, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 955cb1e4-3718-4b96-8e79-81f6088a8794; interfaces file made persistent before reboot; after /sbin/reboot node3 returned with new boot_id d14a339b-e3b0-4269-accd-85a4559f528b; persistent route auto-applied on boot; internet reachability via node1 confirmed, and final node1 conntrack dump shows active translated flows from both node2 and node3 post-restart
